title: New license request: CCBL-1.7
body:
### How license meets inclusion principles

CCBL 1.7 meets the SPDX License List inclusion principles as follows:

**Definitive Factors:**

A) **Not a duplicate**: CCBL 1.7 does not match any existing SPDX license. It is a unique combination of: free personal use, paid commercial use for non-contributors, perpetual free commercial use for qualified contributors, AI-specific restrictions on training/provision, and a 1% revenue donation clause. No existing SPDX license covers this combination. The closest analogs (CC-BY-NC, BSL, SSPL) differ materially — CC-BY-NC lacks the contributor pathway and AI clause; BSL uses delayed open-source; SSPL restricts service deployment, not AI or commercial use per se.

B) **Not OSI-approved, but not required**: CCBL has not been submitted to OSI. This factor permits automatic inclusion for OSI licenses, but does not require OSI approval.

C) **Source code available**: CCBL §2.1 requires that anyone distributing the software must also provide the complete source code. This is not an executable-only license.

D) **Stable, finalized text**: CCBL 1.7 has undergone five rounds of legal review and is published as a finalized version. The text is not in draft or pre-release status. It is available at https://github.com/ccbl-license/ccbl-license/blob/main/LICENSE and archived in the /versions/ directory with both .txt (authoritative) and .md formats.

E) **Versioning commitment**: The license steward (Ignotus Labs) maintains a numbered version archive (1.6 → 1.7) and will not modify published versions. New versions receive new version numbers and are published alongside prior versions.

**Other Evaluation Factors:**

1) **Does not substantially conform to an Open Source Definition**: CCBL intentionally restricts commercial use (§3) and AI training/provision (Appendix A §5). This violates OSD §6 ("No Discrimination Against Fields of Endeavor"). CCBL is a source-available license, not an open source license by OSI/OSD definition. This is acknowledged honestly.

2) **Generic and universal**: CCBL uses standard placeholders (`[year]`, `[copyright holder name]`) and is designed for adoption by any software project. It is not project-specific, company-specific, or tied to any particular ecosystem.

3) **Substantial use / clear adoption plan**: CCBL is a newly published license with active adoption underway. [Project name/URL] uses CCBL 1.7 as its license. The license steward is actively developing a production software project under CCBL and soliciting broader adoption through GitHub Discussions and the official adopters list.

4) **Primarily intended for free distribution, with targeted restrictions**: Although CCBL does not conform to OSD, it is primarily designed for free distribution of software and source code:
   - **Personal and non-commercial use is completely free** (§3.1) — no payment, no restrictions on modification, study, or private redistribution
   - **Contributors receive perpetual free commercial use** (§3.2) — a unique pathway that rewards participation and ensures the ecosystem remains open
   - **Source code is always available** (§2.1) — not locked behind a paywall or delayed release
   The restrictions are **targeted and specific**, not broad: they apply only to two defined activities — (a) commercial use without a qualifying contribution, and (b) using the software to train or provide AI models. These restrictions are the license's core design purpose for sustainable independent development, analogous to how CC-BY-NC targets a specific field (commercial exploitation) while preserving free distribution in all other respects. CCBL's restrictions are narrower than CC-BY-NC in one important respect: CCBL grants free commercial use to contributors, creating an earned pathway that CC-BY-NC entirely denies.

5) **License steward supports inclusion**: The license steward (Ignotus Labs) actively supports and initiated this submission to the SPDX License List.

**Summary**: CCBL fills a recognized gap between fully open source licenses and proprietary/source-available licenses like BSL/SSPL. It provides a legally precise, stable, universally applicable license with a unique contributor pathway. Its inclusion on the SPDX License List would benefit SBOM generation, license compliance scanning, and automated tooling for projects that adopt CCBL — the same utility that SPDX identifiers provide for all listed licenses, regardless of OSI status.


### License Name

Contribution-Commercial-Benevolent License 1.7
